title: Joe Burrow Declares: “We Found a Way to Win” After Years of Struggles – NBC Sports
body:
Cincinnati’s quarterback Joe Burrow told reporters on Tuesday that the Bengals have finally uncovered a “way to win” after a string of frustrating seasons, but the path forward still looks steep. The 27‑year‑old star, who led the Browns to the AFC Championship last year, said the team must first “dig a 13‑0 hole” before they can truly start playing football this season—a nod to the deep work required to rebuild a franchise that has stumbled through three consecutive playoff disappointments.

Burrow’s comments came on the heels of a revealing practice session where the Bengals’ defensive unit, still reeling from a 28‑10 loss to the Baltimore Ravens in Week 7, struggled to contain the opposing offense. The Ravens, who posted a commanding first‑half lead, exposed Cincinnati’s lingering issues in pass rush and secondary coverage. While the offense showed flashes of brilliance, the defense’s inability to stop big plays highlighted why the Bengals have yet to translate talent into consistent victories.

The “13‑0 hole” metaphor, though cryptic, reflects the magnitude of the rebuild Burrow believes is necessary. Analysts point to the fact that Cincinnati entered the offseason with a roster that, on paper, seemed primed for a deep run: a Pro Bowl‑caliber offensive line, a dynamic receiving corps anchored by Ja’Marr Chase, and a defense that had flirted with elite status in 2022. Yet injuries, inconsistent play‑calling, and a lack of depth have left the team scrambling to find a cohesive identity. Burrow’s candid assessment underscores a shift in locker‑room culture, where accountability is being placed not only on the coaching staff but also on the players who must elevate their preparation.

Front office moves have begun to align with Burrow’s urgency. General manager Mike Brown has signaled a willingness to explore trade options for veteran pass‑rushers and to prioritize drafting defensive backs in the upcoming NFL Draft. Meanwhile, head coach Zac Taylor, who survived a turbulent 2023 campaign, has reportedly revamped the defensive scheme, emphasizing more aggressive blitz packages and tighter man coverage to disrupt opposing quarterbacks. The coaching staff’s willingness to adapt, combined with Burrow’s leadership, could be the catalyst needed to close the performance gap.

Nevertheless, the road ahead remains fraught with challenges. Cincinnati’s schedule features back‑to‑back matchups against the Kansas City Chiefs and the Los Angeles Rams—teams that excel at exploiting defensive lapses. Moreover, the Bengals must contend with the lingering effects of key injuries to the offensive line, which have hampered both pass protection and the running game. If the “hole” Burrow references is not filled quickly, the team risks falling into a mid‑season slump that could derail any momentum gained from early‑season adjustments.

Looking forward, the Bengals’ success will hinge on their ability to translate Burrow’s optimism into tangible on‑field results. Early preseason reports suggest a more disciplined defensive unit and an offense that is increasingly comfortable with audibles and tempo changes. If the team can indeed “dig” that 13‑0 hole—building a foundation of depth, resilience, and strategic flexibility—Cincinnati could emerge as a legitimate contender in the AFC by season’s end. The coming weeks will test whether Burrow’s confidence is well‑placed, but the message is clear: the Bengals are ready to do the hard work required to finally win the way they know how.
